title: UNIT 2: VECTORS
notes:
✓ Vector → A physical quantity described by both magnitude and direction.

✓ Scalar → A physical quantity described only by magnitude.

✓ Vectors are used to represent quantities such as displacement, velocity, acceleration and force.

title: 2.1 VECTORS AND TYPES OF VECTORS
notes:
◆ SCALAR VS VECTOR
✓ Scalar → Magnitude only.
✓ Vector → Magnitude + direction.

◆ COMMON VECTORS
Displacement • Velocity • Acceleration • Force • Weight.

◆ GRAPHICAL REPRESENTATION
✓ A vector is represented by a directed arrow drawn to scale.

✓ Arrow length → Represents magnitude.
✓ Arrowhead → Represents direction.

✓ A ruler, protractor and graph paper can be used for scale diagrams.

◆ TYPES OF VECTORS
✓ Collinear → Vectors lying along the same line.
✓ Coplanar → Vectors lying in the same plane.
✓ Parallel → Same direction or parallel lines.
✓ Antiparallel → Opposite directions along parallel lines.
✓ Equal → Same magnitude and direction.
✓ Null/zero vector → Magnitude is zero.
✓ Unit vector → Magnitude is 1 and indicates direction.
✓ Negative vector → Same magnitude as the original but opposite direction.

◆ NEGATIVE VECTOR
✓ If A⃗ is a vector, −A⃗ → Has the same magnitude but opposite direction.

✓ Key idea → Vectors require both magnitude and direction; their direction and orientation determine their classification.

title: 2.2 GRAPHICAL METHOD OF ADDITION OF VECTORS IN TWO DIMENSIONS
notes:
✓ Graphical method → Uses scale diagrams and geometric construction to find vector sums, differences and the resultant.

✓ Resultant vector → The single vector equivalent to the combined effect of the given vectors.

◆ TRIANGLE LAW
✓ Place the second vector head-to-tail with the first.

✓ The vector from the tail of the first to the head of the second → Resultant.

◆ PARALLELOGRAM LAW
✓ Place two vectors tail-to-tail and complete a parallelogram.

✓ The diagonal from the common tail → Resultant.

◆ POLYGON LAW
✓ Used for more than two vectors.

✓ Join vectors head-to-tail in sequence → The vector from the tail of the first to the head of the last is the resultant.

◆ VECTOR SUBTRACTION
✓ A⃗ − B⃗ = A⃗ + (−B⃗)

✓ Reverse the direction of B⃗ → Then add it to A⃗.

◆ SCALE DIAGRAM
✓ Choose a suitable scale → Draw each vector with the correct magnitude and direction → Measure the resultant magnitude and direction.

✓ Graphical methods are useful for visualization but are approximate because measurements are made from diagrams.

title: 2.3 ALGEBRAIC METHOD OF ADDITION OF VECTORS IN TWO DIMENSIONS
notes:
✓ Algebraic/analytical method → Finds vector sums and differences without drawing scale diagrams and gives exact results.

✓ It includes collinear vectors, perpendicular vectors, trigonometric direction, vector components and unit-vector representation.

◆ COLLINEAR VECTORS
✓ Same direction → R = A + B.
✓ Opposite directions → R = A − B, with direction determined by the larger magnitude.

◆ PERPENDICULAR VECTORS
✓ For two perpendicular vectors:
R = √(A² + B²)

✓ Direction relative to the x-axis:
θ = tan⁻¹(Ry/Rx)

◆ RESOLUTION INTO COMPONENTS
✓ A vector can be resolved into perpendicular x- and y-components.

✓ Ax = A cosθ
✓ Ay = A sinθ

✓ Therefore:
A⃗ = Ax i⃗ + Ay j⃗

✓ i⃗ → Unit vector along +x.
✓ j⃗ → Unit vector along +y.

◆ RESULTANT BY COMPONENTS
✓ For R⃗ = A⃗ + B⃗:
Rx = Ax + Bx
Ry = Ay + By
R⃗ = Rx i⃗ + Ry j⃗

◆ MAGNITUDE
✓ R = √(Rx² + Ry²)

◆ DIRECTION
✓ θ = tan⁻¹(Ry/Rx)

◆ UNIT VECTOR
✓ A unit vector → Has magnitude 1 and points in a specified direction.

✓ Unit vector along A:
Â = A⃗/|A⃗|

✓ For a vector A⃗ = Ax i⃗ + Ay j⃗:
|A⃗| = √(Ax² + Ay²)

✓ Key idea → Component methods convert vectors into perpendicular x- and y-parts, making addition and subtraction easier and exact.

title: 2.4 PRODUCT OF VECTORS
notes:
✓ Scalar (dot) product → Combines two vectors and produces a scalar quantity.

✓ It is used to determine angles, vector components and physical quantities such as work and power.

◆ SCALAR / DOT PRODUCT
✓ A⃗ · B⃗ = AB cosθ

✓ θ → Angle between the vectors when placed tail-to-tail.

✓ Using components:
A⃗ · B⃗ = AxBx + AyBy

◆ ANGLE BETWEEN VECTORS
✓ cosθ = (A⃗ · B⃗)/(AB)

✓ θ = cos⁻¹[(A⃗ · B⃗)/(AB)]

◆ DIRECTION COSINES
✓ The cosine of the angle a vector makes with a positive coordinate axis → Direction cosine.

◆ VECTOR COMPONENT ALONG ANOTHER VECTOR
✓ The dot product → Can determine the component of one vector in the direction of another vector.

◆ IMPORTANT DOT-PRODUCT RESULTS
✓ Same direction (θ = 0°) → A⃗·B⃗ = AB, maximum positive value.

✓ Perpendicular (θ = 90°) → A⃗·B⃗ = 0.

✓ Opposite direction (θ = 180°) → A⃗·B⃗ = −AB.

✓ A⃗·A⃗ = A².
✓ A⃗·B⃗ = B⃗·A⃗ → Commutative.
✓ A⃗·(B⃗ + C⃗) = A⃗·B⃗ + A⃗·C⃗ → Distributive.

◆ PHYSICAL APPLICATIONS
✓ Work:
W = F⃗·S⃗ = FS cosθ

✓ Maximum work → Occurs when force and displacement are parallel.

✓ Power:
P = F⃗·v⃗

✓ Key idea → The dot product converts two vectors into a scalar and is especially useful for finding angles, components, work and power.
